topic.name: Dante L1 Prep
topic.title: Dante Certification Level 1 Prep
topic.blurb: Unofficial study companion for Audinate's free Dante Certification Level 1 (3rd Edition): {questions} questions, {cards} flashcards, {guides} guides and {drills} drills covering digital audio and video basics, networking fundamentals, Dante products and Dante Controller.

tracks.label: Dante Certification Level 1 (3rd Edition)
tracks.summary: Free, self-paced online course plus final certification test (exam length not public); entry level for AV pros, integrators and IT staff working with single-switch Dante networks.

domains.name: Dante & Audinate Ecosystem
domains.description: Who Audinate is, what makes Dante a complete AV-over-IP platform (chipsets, software implementations, management tools). Official Chapter 2.

domains.name: Digital Audio Fundamentals
domains.description: Sampling, sample rate, bit depth and encoding as they apply to Dante. Taught in the Level 1 'digital audio basics' chapter referenced by the Chapter 4 transcript; its chapter number is not published.

domains.name: Dante Audio Products
domains.description: Dante audio chipsets and software implementations, Dante AVIO adapter families, Dante Virtual Soundcard (incl. DVS Pro) and Dante Via. Official Chapter 4.

domains.name: Digital Video Fundamentals
domains.description: Resolution, frame rate, compression, EDID and HDCP basics. Taught in the Level 1 'video basics' chapter referenced by the Chapter 6 transcript; its chapter number is not published.

domains.name: Dante AV
domains.description: Dante AV Ultra, Dante AV-A and Dante AV-H, Dante Studio (Video Tx/Rx/Viewer), latency, EDID, HDCP and bandwidth settings. Official Chapter 6.

domains.name: Dante Functional Categories & First Network
domains.description: The four functional categories (discovery, clocking, subscriptions, latency), building a single-switch Dante network, audio breakaway. Official Chapter 7.

domains.name: Networking Fundamentals
domains.description: MAC and IP addressing and network topologies (daisy chain, single switch) as named in the official Level 1 course descriptions; chapter number not published.

domains.name: Latency
domains.description: What Dante latency is and how it is set and monitored. Taught in the Level 1 'introduction to latency' chapter referenced by the Chapter 10 transcript; chapter number not published.

domains.name: Dante Controller
domains.description: Network interface selection, naming conventions, Network/Device views, routing matrix subscriptions, status icons and tabs (Device Info, Clock Status, Network Status, Events). Official Chapter 10.

exam.disclaimer: Audinate does not publish the Level 1 test's question count, time limit or pass mark, so scores here are a study signal only, not a prediction of your certification result.

roadmap.title: Your path to Dante Level 1
roadmap.intro: Level 1 is free and self-paced. Work through the official course on the Dante training portal, use this app to drill each domain, then sit the final certification test on the portal.
roadmap.footer: Enrollment is free with a GetDante account: getdante.com/certify. Program details: Dante Certification Program.

tracks.note: 3rd Edition (launched autumn 2025). Certificate valid three years.
items: Enroll in Dante Certification Level 1 (3rd Edition) from the portal catalog
Install Dante Controller (free, Windows and macOS) to follow along
Work through every course chapter and its quizzes
Reach your readiness target in each domain in this app
Pass the final certification test on the portal
Download your certificate from My Progress > Certificates
If you hold CTS, CTS-D, CTS-I or ANP, submit the course to AVIXA for renewal units

notebooklm.notebookTitle: Dante Certification Level 1 — Prep Hub sources
prompts: Write a one-page guide to Dante Controller for a first-time Level 1 candidate: choosing the network interface, naming devices and channels before subscribing, making and breaking subscriptions, and reading the common status icons. Use only the sources.
Explain Dante's four functional categories (discovery, clocking, subscriptions, latency) with a worked example of building a single-switch network, as covered in Level 1 Chapter 7.
Compare Dante AV Ultra, Dante AV-A and Dante AV-H in a table (use case, video handling, typical venue), then explain how Dante Studio's Video Tx, Video Rx and Video Viewer fit in.
Write a guide to the Dante audio product family for a beginner: AVIO adapter categories with one use case each, and when to choose Dante Virtual Soundcard versus Dante Via.
List every fact in the sources about sample rate, latency and channel counts (e.g. DVS channel limits at 48 kHz vs 96 kHz) as flashcard-ready question/answer pairs, citing the chapter each came from.

Describe three Level 1 troubleshooting scenarios from the sources (renamed device breaking a subscription, sample rate mismatch, wrong network interface) with symptoms in Dante Controller and the fix.

researchNotes:
VERIFIED (live web, 2026-10-13): Dante Certification Level 1 exists as named; the current version is the 3rd Edition, a full rewrite of Levels 1-3 (getdante.com program page, modified 2026-08-03; Audinate press release dated 8 Oct 2025). Programme ladder on the official page: Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, plus Dante Domain Manager Administrator; the support FAQ also describes Dante Mastery, a 4-day in-person class. Only Level 1 is in scope, so the dossier has a single track (L1, prerequisite none; no prerequisite is stated for Level 1 anywhere).

NO OFFICIAL BLUEPRINT: Audinate publishes no exam content outline, no domain weights and no task list for Level 1. `duties` is therefore absent and readiness falls back to per-domain scoring. Domains are taken from the official course structure: the five chapters Audinate publishes publicly (Ch2 Who is Audinate & What is Dante, Ch4 Introduction to Dante Audio, Ch6 Introduction to Dante AV, Ch7 A Simple Demonstration, Ch10 Introduction to Dante Controller), plus four topics the official course material itself names as Level 1 chapters or topics but whose chapter numbers and exact titles are not public: digital audio basics (referenced in the Ch4 transcript), video basics (Ch6 transcript), introduction to latency (Ch10 transcript), and networking fundamentals incl. MAC/IP addressing and topologies (program page; AVIXA's listing of the course). Inferred, NOT verified: Ch1 is a programme introduction (Ch2 opens 'now that you know about the Dante certification program'), Ch3 is probably digital audio basics, Ch5 probably video basics, Ch8-9 probably networking and latency. The total number of Level 1 chapters is unknown (at least 10).

GATED: The full course, chapter quizzes and the final certification test live on the TalentLMS portal (getdante.com/certify -> audinate.talentlms.com), which needs a free GetDante account sign-in. Nothing behind the login was viewed. Not published publicly and therefore NOT recorded: test question count, time limit, pass mark, attempt limits/retake policy, ID or proctoring rules. exam.passMark 70, simQuestions 50 and simMinutes 60 are app practice defaults chosen by the research stage, not Audinate figures; the disclaimer says so. Isaac (or anyone with a GetDante account) can fill these in by enrolling and reading the test instructions.

FEES: Free. Program page says 'Enroll Free Today'; press release says courses are free for all three levels. No currency applies; no price was estimated.

VALIDITY: Three years from award (program 3rd Edition page, press release, support FAQ). The 'Where can I get my certificates?' FAQ adds that some certificates are valid 3-5 years and that a new course edition can mark older certificates inactive/expired.

CONFLICTS (recorded, not resolved):
1. AVIXA RUs for Level 1: program page and press release say 5.5 RUs (CTS, CTS-D, CTS-I, ANP); AVIXA's own course listing also shows 5.5. The support FAQ 'Do Dante Certification courses qualify for AVIXA CTS Renewal Units?' (updated 2026-05-11) gives 'typical' values of ~2 / ~4 / ~6 RUs for Levels 1/2/3 and tells readers to check with AVIXA. The FAQ values look like legacy figures; the app should state 5.5 and cite the program page.
2. 3rd Edition launch date: support FAQ says September 2025; press release is dated 8 October 2025; the 3rd Edition web page was first published 26 Aug 2025 and the public chapter videos 3 Oct 2025.
3. CEUs: program page lists 3.25 CEDIA CEUs for Level 1; no other source mentions it.

EDITION RISK: The 2nd Edition remains available online in non-English languages, and many third-party study notes describe the 1st/2nd Edition. Build content only from 3rd Edition sources. A 2019 Level 1 introduction PDF found via search is 1st/2nd Edition material and was deliberately not used.

UNREACHABLE: audinate.com/learning/... pages returned HTTP 403; support.getdante.com blocks plain HTTP clients and was read through a headless browser render.

CONTENT SPLIT (265 questions, no official weights, so weighted by apparent course emphasis and testability): Dante Controller 45; Networking Fundamentals 35; Digital Audio Fundamentals 35; Dante Functional Categories & First Network 30; Dante AV 30; Latency 25; Dante Audio Products 25; Digital Video Fundamentals 25; Dante & Audinate Ecosystem 15. Domains whose chapters are not public (digital audio, video, networking, latency) must be written from standard concepts that the public chapters reference, and checked against the gated course by someone enrolled before shipping. Drills: 10 Dante Controller troubleshooting scenarios (unresolved subscription after rename, sample rate mismatch, wrong NIC, video resolution/frame-rate switching delays, etc.). No library: Audinate publishes no public 3rd Edition PDFs for Level 1.
